name: a coordinate reference resolves to the cell it names
geml:
=== table {#fy format=csv header=1}
Segment, Q1
Cloud, 8
Edge, 3
===

Q1 is [[#fy[1]["Q1"]]].

name: a coordinate reference may name a whole row
geml:
=== table {#fy format=csv header=1}
Segment, Q1
Cloud, 8
Edge, 3
===

Row: [[#fy[2]]].

name: a coordinate reference may name a summary row, which a `view` declares
geml:
=== table {#fy format=csv header=1}
Segment, Q1
Cloud, 8
Edge, 3
===

=== view {#total src=#fy summary="Segment = 'Total'; Q1 = sum(Q1)"}
===

Total: [[#total[summary]["Q1"]]].

name: a coordinate reference may name a column: it resolves, and carries no value of its own
geml:
=== table {#fy format=csv header=1}
Segment, Q1
Cloud, 8
Edge, 3
===

All: [[#fy["Q1"]]].

name: an inline projection of a coordinate is its value
geml:
=== table {#fy format=csv header=1}
Segment, Q1
Cloud, 8
Edge, 3
===

Projected: ![[#fy[1]["Q1"]]].

name: `#meta` names the merged namespace, the first definition winning
geml:
=== meta
title = "First"
===

=== meta
title = "Second"
owner = "ops"
===

By [[#meta["title"]]] of [[#meta["owner"]]].

name: a value tree resolves by key and by index
a row reads as its cells joined by ", ", whatever delimiter the body was written in
geml:
=== table {#t format=csv header=1 delim=";"}
A;B
1;2
===

Row: [[#t[1]]].

name: a reference to a value-tree node that holds more nodes resolves and carries no value of its own
a header-less table names its columns by letter
geml:
=== table {#t format=csv header=0}
Cloud, 8
Edge, 3
===

B2: [[#t[2]["B"]]].

name: a row index past the last row does not resolve
geml:
=== table {#t format=csv header=1}
Segment, Q1
Cloud, 8
===

X: [[#t[2]]].

name: a row with more cells than the table has columns is cut to the header's width, with a warning
geml:
=== table {#t format=csv header=1}
A, B
1, 2, 3
===

name: a row with fewer cells is padded with empty cells, with a warning
geml:
=== table {#t format=csv header=1}
A, B
4
===

name: a header-less table is as wide as its widest row; a shorter row is padded, with a warning
geml:
=== table {#t format=csv header=0}
1
2, 3
===

name: the visual form's rows are held to the header's width the same way
a header-less visual grid is as wide as its widest body row
a data body splits on the delimiter and on nothing else, so a quoted comma splits too
geml:
=== table {#t format=csv header=1}
Segment, Q1
"Cloud, EU", 8
===

name: a visual cell holds a pipe written `\|`, code spans included; every other pipe separates
geml:
=== table {#t}
| Key | Values |
|---|---|
| `order` | `asc \| desc` |
| sep | a \| b |
===

Row: [[#t[1]]].

name: a cell's text is trimmed of White_Space: a no-break space and NEL go, U+FEFF is content and stays
geml:
=== table {#t format=csv header=1}
A,B
 x ,y
﻿z,w
===

name: the visual form's cells are trimmed of the same White_Space
